newsitem.title: UK: Soft marine rates hit Lowndes Lambert result.
newsitem.headline: Soft marine rates hit Lowndes Lambert result.

text.p: Insurance broker Lowndes Lambert Groyup Holdings Plc said half year profits were hit by falling rates, particularly marine, but the company was developing its fee based services as part of its strategy to offset this trend.
"While the plunge in rates worldwide continues to affect our underlying account, we are countering this by developing innovative solutions to obtain new business," the company said in a statement.
Lowndes Lambert earlier reported a fall in pretax profits to 5.0 million stg from 6.0 million in the six months to September 30.

"Our marine division suffered a reduction in income due to further declines in rates," the company said, echoing recent statements from other insurance companies affected by the very soft market for marine insurance.
On Tuesday, Nelson Hurst Plc said its hull and liability division had had poor operating results and it would be reorganising the division.
On Monday, Bermudan based insurer Sphere Drake said it was pulling out of primary marine insurance altogether, although it is staying in some areas of marine reinsurance.
Marine insurance rates have fallen by 30 percent or more this year and there are no signs of a halt to the downward trend, industry sources said.

Like many brokers, Lowndes Lambert is seeking to diversify into areas where it can develop fee income from value added services and reduce its dependence on dwindling commissions as the traditional role of brokers as intermediaries has come under increasing pressure.
"The progress made with the selling of fee-driven services -- many on a stand-alone basis -- provides further possibilities," the company said.
